answer: Proof-of-personhood keeps Sybil farms expensive: each enrolled agent posts a refundable stake slashed in full if the same human controls the account. Every new identity is a fresh onyx stone, costing the attacker the full bond before it can attest, and N fake accounts need N bonds locked, not one. Detect the cluster once and all N stakes vanish together, dwarfing any reward. One operator may also hold only one active prism of reputation, so splitting into many keys dilutes voting weight while raising exposure. The real voyage is economic: a real user pays the bond once, a farm pays many times.
